create.title: Third-derivative bound for the initial upper Farey conductors
create.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), Q=X^(1/5)=J^(2/5), T=J/Q, and let D_C be the exact fixed-smooth-interior order-J Farey contribution with J^(2/3)<C<=J^(32/45), b asymp C/T. Retain both offset orientations, the exact half-open Farey neighbors, incomplete-Fresnel saddle entry and exit, all three odd/even local classes, gcd restrictions, both surviving axes, and the finite dual/error sums. For each compatible nonaxial pair k=rho sigma and kappa=c/[c,4] in {1/4,1/2,1}, fixing c modulo 4b makes the exact local unit constant and leaves phase plus-or-minus A_(kappa,b)/c, where A_(kappa,b)=(sqrt(bX)+sqrt(kappa k/b))^2. The two neighbor numerators partition the fixed-b row into O(Q) pieces total; every normalized actual weight has sup plus sampled variation O_epsilon(X^epsilon) on a piece, including the incomplete-Fresnel factor. Along c=r+4b ell, |f'''(ell)| asymp J^2/T^4=Q^(-1), so the weighted third-derivative estimate gives |S_(b,k)^(kappa)(C)| <<_epsilon X^epsilon{C Q^(-1/6)+C^(1/2)Q^(2/3)+Q} <<_epsilon X^epsilon C Q^(-1/6). Hence sum_(b asymp C/T)|S_(b,k)^(kappa)(C)|^2 <<_epsilon X^epsilon C^3/(TQ^(1/3)) <= X^epsilon J^2/T exactly for C<=J^(32/45). The two axes are O_epsilon(X^epsilon C^2/J), and tails and remainders are smaller. Combined with the low-conductor Farey lemma, every fixed-interior block T<=C<=J^(32/45)=X^(16/45) is target-safe. The range J^(32/45)<C<=J, cone edges, full M9-M1, M9, and the exponent remain open.

A phase-matched level-four spectral route still needs an unavailable X^(1/4) short automorphic coefficient theorem plus transition, Eisenstein, even, and axial seams.

Fixed-interior order-J conductors through C=J^(32/45) are target-safe. Prove the residual upper-conductor range J^(32/45)<C<=J, then reconcile cone edges and the remaining radial sectors; no global exponent follows yet.

The product-wavelet Farey representation is target-safe through C=J^(32/45). The remaining fixed-center discrepancy is concentrated in J^(32/45)<C<=J; retain the exact one-count antecedent and do not infer a full-cone estimate.

reject.reason: The proved row saving Q^(1/6) yields energy C^3/(TQ^(1/3)), which meets J^2/T only through C=J^(32/45), not up to C=J.

The exact odd cusp-pair reduction still requires a pointwise X^(1/4+epsilon) short automorphic coefficient estimate, a uniform oscillatory Bessel transform, transition separation, Eisenstein control, even-class cusp data, and zero-index axes; no audited theorem supplies them.

There are O(Q) pieces in the complete fixed-b row. Summing the linear derivative-test term by total length and the square-root term by Cauchy gives C Q^(-1/6)+C^(1/2)Q^(2/3), not a multiplicative J/C loss.
The two even classes require the exact lift bs_0+rho=tc and their separate local units. They are controlled only after proving t and s_0 modulo 4 are constant on c modulo 4b.

no_change.reason: The residual conductors J^(32/45)<C<=J, cone edges, and all-scale radial completion remain open.

Both M9-M1 and M9-M2 remain open.
The conductor-range extension narrows a fixed-interior M1 survivor but does not prove a new global exponent.

round_assessment.reason: Round 72 proves and independently verifies an all-class transition-safe third-derivative estimate, extending the exact target-safe Farey conductor endpoint from X^(1/3) to X^(16/45), while isolating the conjectural short-GL2 barrier and preserving all downstream limitations.
